A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BinaryDM and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, and appendices. Renamed sections and relocated results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDIM/LDM generation experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and a 50-person user study.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds quantization, architectural-control, and training-budget results in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The default dual-basis LMB, PCA-based LRM objective, and progressive initialization remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a limited extension to three- and four-basis LMB variants (Table 12). Relabeling the default weights from 1 to 1.1 bits does not itself establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: All five image datasets and the unconditional/conditional generation tasks are retained, including relocated FFHQ results. However, v2 removes v1 Appendix C's human evaluation of image quality and condition-image consistency, involving 50 users and 20 image sets.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 newly evaluates Q-DM and TDQ on LSUN-Bedrooms; Q-DM was previously only cited. Table 18 adds EfficientDM to ImageNet comparisons, while Tables 16–17 introduce mixed-precision LSQ and QALoRA controls. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparisons beyond v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces detailed LMB placement/basis-count sweeps, higher-precision LRM controls, and ImageNet training budgets from 10K to 150K steps. Appendix B.1 also revises reported efficiency accounting from scaled FLOPs to OPs combining BOPs/64 with full-precision FLOPs. The original 50,000-sample generation evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already ablated component inclusion, LMB scope, PCA reduction, and initialization. v2 retains these and adds head/tail versus central placement, finer placement sweeps, additional binary bases, higher-precision distillation, mixed-precision controls, QALoRA training, and training-duration analyses (Tables 10–18). These substantially deepen tests of the design rationale.

E5.justification: v2 checklist item 7 newly states that random seeds were fixed for all experiments. It supplies neither seed values nor repeated-run counts or newly defined uncertainty estimates; this disclosure does not establish additional runs or statistical significance.

E6.justification: Most original generation scores are retained. The main ImageNet/DDIM result changes from IS 163.14/FID 10.00 to 190.36/10.40; the earlier values reappear at 150K steps in v2 Table 18, so a matched-setting gain is not established. Numerous new comparison/ablation results, revised costs such as LDM-4 BinaryDM's 40.8 to 42.1 MB size, and removal of user-study outcomes substantially change the evidence.

T1.justification: The LRM projection definition changes multiplication order: v1 Equation 12 places the PCA matrix before the features, whereas v2 Equation 11 places it afterward while retaining the stated tensor shapes. This is a localized mathematical revision; the principal derivations remain and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main LMB/LRM contributions and first-binarization claim remain. However, the abstract, introduction, and conclusion now describe 1.1-bit rather than 1-bit weights and revise headline savings from 16.0× FLOPs/27.1× storage to 9.3× OPs/24.8× storage, narrowing the quantitative efficiency claim.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds substantive interpretations of placement tradeoffs, diminishing returns from additional bases, and LRM's weaker FID performance than MSE at four-bit weights. It also attributes differences from EfficientDM partly to full-model training and access to original data. Section 4.3 newly identifies generic layerwise activation quantization as a limitation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies CPU/A800 80GB hardware, 20-step DDIM sampling for ImageNet, and training-step/time pairs. Its checklist promises supplementary code, without establishing accessible code in the supplied material. Existing batch sizes, approximate training duration, and relative learning-rate descriptions remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to MeliusNet, attribution-rank-preserving mixed-precision quantization, and GWQ to support efficiency accounting. It also expands discussion of differences from EfficientDM. The broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title drops the BinaryDM prefix, and the abstract and portions of the introduction and method receive targeted rewrites. Method headings change, Appendix B separates quantitative results from additional analyses, and a checklist is appended. The main narrative sequence and substantial portions of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text to a single-column layout, redraws the overview, adds an accuracy-efficiency plot, and splits or relocates major tables. Original sample images are retained and rearranged, while user-study plots disappear. Some revised captions incorrectly describe eight- and 32-bit activation panels as four-bit, including Figures 10–11.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central accuracy-efficiency argument through placement and matched mixed-precision controls that test whether gains merely reflect extra precision. Explicit 1.1-bit reporting, fuller operation accounting, and acknowledgment of EfficientDM's different training/data access address important weaknesses in v1's comparisons. Removing the user study and introducing misleading sample captions are losses, but the improvements to core validation and transparency are substantial.
